rationale: PINS that a parameter shadows a same-named file-level symbol, and — just as importantly — that it does not silence a genuine reference. A PARAMETER is the most local binding a function has: it shadows every module- and class-level name for the whole body, so a read of that name resolves to the parameter and never to the file symbol that shares it. The reference pass resolves by NAME, and it already knew the principle — `locals` holds a function's destructuring patterns and its `const`/`let` declarators — but a parameter was missing from that set. The result was a false edge in the direction that hides rather than shouts: with `interface Deps { root: string }` in the file, `function f(root: string) { return root }` published `f->root`, so the graph recorded the function as referencing an interface property it never touches. Measured: 160 of 2,880 `references` over 700 tracked files (5.6%), led by the names most likely to collide (`n`, `root`, `name`, `src`, `node`, `source`); 229 removed across a 1500-file A/B, every one of them justified as a parameter of the referencing symbol, with 0 added. All four parameter forms are pinned: a bare identifier (the broken one), a destructured parameter and a rest parameter (both already handled, because the existing pattern branch sees them — pinned so that stays true), and a parameter shadowing a FUNCTION. The three genuine references are pinned with equal weight, because the opposite mistake — seeding `locals` too eagerly — would silence real edges, and a graph that under-claims is as wrong as one that over-claims.

expectRelationships.note: GENUINE, and the pin that makes the negatives meaningful. The module const `root` really is referenced here — there is no parameter of that name in scope — so this edge must survive. A fix that seeded `locals` with every name mentioned anywhere would pass a negatives-only fixture and quietly gut the reference graph.

forbidRelationships.note: THE PIN. `root` here is the function's own parameter. Pre-fix this edge existed because an interface property of the same name is declared in the file, so name-based resolution published it. Same for `byParam->name` below.
A parameter shadowing a FUNCTION name: the call is to the parameter, not to the declared helper.
